proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(c=(a,x)\). Since every coordinate of \(q^0_c\) is positive and the support contains at least two distinct values, \(\sigma_c^2(q^0)>0\). Define
\[
m_{c\ell}=\frac{q^0_{c\ell}(y_\ell-\mu_c(q^0))}{\sigma_c^2(q^0)}.
\]
Then \(\sum_\ell m_{c\ell}=0\) and \(\sum_\ell y_\ell m_{c\ell}=1\). Thus the cellwise map from the simplex tangent to its mean is onto. Because \(\operatorname{rank}(F)=d\) by \(\mathrm{ass:menu\text{-}rank}\), the matrix \(A_{\mathrm{map}}=[-F\;F]\) has row rank \(d\), and hence \(A_{\mathrm{tan}}=A_{\mathrm{map}}B_{\mathrm{mean}}\) is onto.

For fixed \(C_v\), the set \(\mathcal H\times\{v:\lVert v\rVert\le C_v\}\) is compact and the map \((h,v)\mapsto S_0h+Wv\) is linear and continuous. Consequently
\[
C_s(C_v):=\sup_{h\in\mathcal H,\,\lVert v\rVert\le C_v}\lVert S_0h+Wv\rVert_\infty<\infty.
\]
If \(n>(C_s(C_v)/\delta_q)^2\), then, coordinatewise,
\[
q_{n,ax\ell}(h,v)
=q^0_{ax\ell}+\frac{s(h,v)_{ax\ell}}{\sqrt n}
\ge q^0_{ax\ell}-\frac{C_s(C_v)}{\sqrt n}
>q^0_{ax\ell}-\delta_q\ge\eta.
\]
Moreover \(s(h,v)\in\mathcal E\), so every cell of \(q_n(h,v)\) sums to one. The three defining conditions in \(\mathrm{def:saturated\text{-}model}\), together with \(\mathrm{ass:eta\text{-}interior}\), therefore give \(P_{p,q_n(h,v)}\in\mathcal M_\eta(p)\), uniformly on the displayed compact set.

Linearity of the mean and the definitions of \(S_0,W\) give
\[
\sqrt n\{\theta_p(q_n(h,v))-\theta_p(q^0)\}
=A_{\mathrm{tan}}s(h,v)
=A_{\mathrm{tan}}S_0h+A_{\mathrm{tan}}Wv=h.
\]
The tied-baseline condition \(\theta_p(q^0)=0\) then proves \(\sqrt n\,\theta_p(q_n(h,v))=h\).

It remains to verify the advertised nuisance coverage. For arbitrary \(h\in\mathcal H\) and bounded \(u\in\mathbb R^{K-d}\), let the desired cell-mean tangent have treatment blocks
\[
b_0=0,\qquad b_1=Qh+Nu.
\]
The cellwise construction above supplies \(s_b\in\mathcal E\) with \(B_{\mathrm{mean}}s_b=b\). Since \(FQ=I_d\) and \(FN=0\),
\[
A_{\mathrm{tan}}s_b=A_{\mathrm{map}}b=F(Qh+Nu)=h.
\]
Thus \(s_b-S_0h\in\ker(A_{\mathrm{tan}})=\operatorname{im}(W)\), so the bijectivity of \(W\) gives a unique \(v=W^{-1}(s_b-S_0h)\); boundedness follows from finite-dimensional continuity. Similarly, choosing \(b_0=b_1=c\) gives every common-arm-mean direction, and adding arbitrary cellwise \(k_c\) satisfying \(\sum_\ell k_{c\ell}=\sum_\ell y_\ell k_{c\ell}=0\) gives every zero-mean shape direction. These subspaces have dimensions \(K\), \(K-d\), and \(2K(L-2)\), whose sum is \(2K(L-1)-d=\dim\ker(A_{\mathrm{tan}})\); hence none is omitted.

For a fixed cell \(c=(a,x)\), define
\[
m_{c\ell}=\frac{q^0_{c\ell}(y_\ell-\mu_c(q^0))}{\sigma_c^2(q^0)}.
\]
As \(\sum_\ell m_{c\ell}=0\) and \(\sum_\ell y_\ell m_{c\ell}=1\), every simplex tangent \(s_c\) has the unique decomposition
\[
s_c=b_cm_c+k_c,\qquad b_c=\sum_\ell y_\ell s_{c\ell},\qquad
\sum_\ell k_{c\ell}=\sum_\ell y_\ell k_{c\ell}=0.
\]
Under the multinomial Fisher inner product,
\[
\sum_\ell\frac{m_{c\ell}k_{c\ell}}{q^0_{c\ell}}
=\frac{1}{\sigma_c^2(q^0)}\sum_\ell(y_\ell-\mu_c(q^0))k_{c\ell}=0,
\qquad
\sum_\ell\frac{m_{c\ell}^2}{q^0_{c\ell}}=\frac{1}{\sigma_c^2(q^0)}.
\]
Annotation ignorability makes an observed label in cell \(c\) occur with probability \(p_xe_{ax}r_{ax}\), while an unlabelled record has zero outcome score. Hence the residual mean tangent is Fisher-orthogonal to every shape tangent and its information is \(p_xe_{ax}r_{ax}/\sigma_c^2(q^0)\), exactly the corresponding diagonal entry of \(I_r\).

All entries of \(I_r\) are positive: \(p_x,e_{ax},r_{ax}>0\), and eta positivity on a support with distinct values makes \(\sigma_c^2(q^0)>0\). Direct block multiplication yields
\[
A_{\mathrm{map}}I_r^{-1}A_{\mathrm{map}}^\top
=\sum_{x=1}^K\sum_{a=0}^1
\frac{p_x\sigma^2_{ax}(q^0)}{e_{ax}r_{ax}}d_xd_x^\top
=\Sigma(r).
\]
Since \(A_{\mathrm{map}}\) has row rank \(d\), this matrix is positive definite. Substitution of \(T_r=I_r^{-1}A_{\mathrm{map}}^\top\Sigma(r)^{-1}\) now gives
\[
A_{\mathrm{map}}T_r
=A_{\mathrm{map}}I_r^{-1}A_{\mathrm{map}}^\top\Sigma(r)^{-1}=I_d,
\]
and
\[
T_r^\top I_rT_r
=\Sigma(r)^{-1}A_{\mathrm{map}}I_r^{-1}A_{\mathrm{map}}^\top\Sigma(r)^{-1}
=\Sigma(r)^{-1}.
\]
This also proves that the probability lift \(\mathcal T_r\) has contrast \(A_{\mathrm{tan}}\mathcal T_rb=b\) and information \(J_r(\mathcal T_rb,\mathcal T_rc)=b^\top\Sigma(r)^{-1}c\).

Fix \(C_v<\infty\), and write \(s=s(h,v)\). The membership conclusion follows from \(\mathrm{thm:local\text{-}chart\text{-}membership}\). On its compact parameter set there is a finite \(A_C\) such that
\[
\max_{a,x,\ell}\left|\frac{s_{ax\ell}}{q^0_{ax\ell}}\right|\le A_C,
\]
because \(q^0_{ax\ell}\ge\eta>0\). Conditional on \(\mathscr P_n\), the annotation rate \(\widehat r_n\) is fixed. For one main-wave observation its likelihood ratio relative to \(q^0\) equals one when \(R=0\), and when \(R=1,Y^{\mathrm{obs}}=y_\ell\) it equals
\[
\frac{q^0_{AX\ell}+s_{AX\ell}/\sqrt n}{q^0_{AX\ell}}
=1+\frac{g_s(O)}{\sqrt n}.
\]
Annotation ignorability is what cancels the annotation factor. If \(A_C/\sqrt n\le1/2\), Taylor's formula with a uniform third-derivative bound gives
\[
\log(1+z)=z-\frac{z^2}{2}+r(z),\qquad |r(z)|\le\frac{2}{3}|z|^3,\qquad |z|\le\frac12.
\]
Summing this identity gives
\[
\log\Lambda_{n,\mathrm{main}}(s)
=\Delta_n(s)-\frac1{2n}\sum_{i=1}^ng_s(O_i)^2+R_n(s),
\qquad \sup_s|R_n(s)|\le\frac{2A_C^3}{3\sqrt n}.
\]
Choose a basis of the finite-dimensional space \(\mathcal E\). Every product of two basis scores is bounded. Conditional Chebyshev bounds for their sample averages, followed by the assumed locally uniform convergence \(\widehat r_n\to r\), imply
\[
\sup_{h\in\mathcal H,\lVert v\rVert\le C_v}
\left|\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^ng_s(O_i)^2-J_{\widehat r_n}(s,s)\right|=o_P(1).
\]
This proves the stated uniform remainder. Applied to the vector of basis scores, \(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}dimensional\text{-}lindeberg\text{-}feller}\) applies conditionally because the summands are centered, uniformly bounded, and their covariance converges to the matrix of \(J_r\). Linearity in the basis coordinates upgrades this to uniform finite-coordinate convergence over the compact tangent set.

For \(t\in\ker(A_{\mathrm{tan}})\), the information calculation gives
\[
J_r(\Pi_rs,t)=J_r(\mathcal T_rA_{\mathrm{tan}}s,t)
=(A_{\mathrm{tan}}s)^\top\Sigma(r)^{-1}A_{\mathrm{tan}}t=0,
\]
and \(A_{\mathrm{tan}}\Pi_rs=A_{\mathrm{tan}}s\). Thus \(\Pi_r\) is the \(J_r\)-orthogonal projection onto the least-favourable contrast space. Moreover, for every \(b\in\mathbb R^d\),
\[
J_r(\mathcal T_rb,s(h,v))=b^\top\Sigma(r)^{-1}h,
\qquad J_r(\mathcal T_rb,\mathcal T_rc)=b^\top\Sigma(r)^{-1}c.
\]
The proved joint likelihood and score convergence imply that, under the local law, \(\Delta_n\circ\mathcal T_r\) has limiting mean \(\Sigma(r)^{-1}h\) and covariance \(\Sigma(r)^{-1}\). Therefore \(U_{n,r}=\Sigma(r)(\Delta_n\circ\mathcal T_r)\Rightarrow N(h,\Sigma(r))\), uniformly on the fixed bounded fiber.

For a fully labelled pilot record the local likelihood ratio is \(1+g_s/\sqrt n\), and hence
\[
E_0\Lambda_{n,\mathrm{pilot}}(s)^2
=\left(1+\frac{J_1(s,s)}n\right)^{m_n}
\le \exp\{m_nJ_1(s,s)/n\}=1+o(1)
\]
uniformly on the compact tangent set, by \(m_n/n\to0\). Thus its total-variation contribution is at most one half of the square root of the displayed second-moment excess and vanishes. Conditional on every pilot realization,
\[
E_0\{\Lambda_{n,\mathrm{main}}(s)^2\mid\mathscr P_n\}
=\left(1+\frac{J_{\widehat r_n}(s,s)}n\right)^n
\le e^{J_1(s,s)},
\]
because \(0\le\widehat r_{n,ax}\le1\). The full likelihood vectors for any finite collection of local states are therefore uniformly square-integrable, regardless of discontinuities of the pilot selector.

For a finite prior \(\sum_{\nu=1}^Nw_\nu\delta_{h_\nu}\), take the allowed least-favourable tangents \(\mathcal T_rh_\nu\). Compactness of \(\mathcal H\) and continuity of \(\mathcal T_r\) place all of them in one fixed nuisance ball. Under the baseline law the optimal Bayes regret in the finite experiment is exactly
\[
E_0\min_{j\in[M]}\sum_{\nu=1}^Nw_\nu\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}(h_\nu,j)\Lambda_n(\mathcal T_rh_\nu).
\]
The integrand is continuous in the likelihood vector and is bounded by \(2\sup_{h\in\mathcal H}\lVert h\rVert_\infty\sum_\nu w_\nu\Lambda_n(\mathcal T_rh_\nu)\). Joint likelihood convergence and the preceding square-integrability therefore give convergence of its expectation. In the Gaussian limit the likelihood vector is that generated by \(Z\sim N(h,\Sigma(r))\), so the limit is precisely the asserted Gaussian Bayes regret. This proves the finite-prior transfer without claiming total-variation convergence of the discrete and Gaussian experiments.

Fix \(r\in\mathcal R_B\). Positivity in \(\mathrm{lem:efficient\text{-}contrast\text{-}information}\) makes \(I_r\) and \(\Sigma(r)\) positive definite. Consider the Gaussian cell-mean experiment \(Y_G\sim N(b,I_r^{-1})\) with nuisance fiber \(A_{\mathrm{map}}b=h\). The statistic \(Z=A_{\mathrm{map}}Y_G\) has law \(N(h,\Sigma(r))\), so rules based on \(Z\) prove that the full-fiber value is at most \(L(r)\). On the least-favourable slice \(b=T_rh\), define \(E_G=Y_G-T_rA_{\mathrm{map}}Y_G\). The information identities imply
\[
\operatorname{Cov}(E_G,Z)=I_r^{-1}A_{\mathrm{map}}^\top-T_r\Sigma(r)=0,
\qquad E(E_G)=T_rh-T_rh=0.
\]
Joint Gaussianity makes \(E_G\) independent of \(Z\), and its law is independent of \(h\). Hence it is ancillary on this slice and cannot lower the minimax regret below the \(Z\)-game. The reverse inequality follows, proving equality with \(L(r)\).

For existence, let \(\mu\) be any Gaussian probability measure equivalent to Lebesgue measure and represent a rule as \((\delta_1,\ldots,\delta_M)\in L^\infty(\mu)^M\) with nonnegative coordinates summing to one. This set is weak-star compact by \(\mathrm{lem:weak\text{-}star\text{-}rule\text{-}compactness}\), and each risk is weak-star continuous because the corresponding normal density times the bounded regret belongs to \(L^1(\mu)\). The set of probability measures on compact \(\mathcal H\) is compact and convex. Applying \(\mathrm{lem:sion\text{-}minimax}\) to rule and prior yields a minimax rule and equality of the minimax value with the supremum of Bayes values over all priors.

Let \(U=\sup_{h\in\mathcal H}\lVert h\rVert_\infty\) and \(R_0=2U\). Compactness of \(\mathcal R_B\), positivity of \(r_{ax}\ge\rho\), and full row rank give constants \(0<\lambda_0\le\lambda_{\min}\{\Sigma(r)\}\) for all \(r\). For densities \(p,q\), partitioning over \(\{p\ge q\}\), applying the log-sum inequality on the two partition cells, and differentiating the resulting Bernoulli divergence gives \(d_{\mathrm{TV}}(P,Q)^2\le D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P,Q)/2\). Applying this proved scalar inequality to equal-covariance normals and using the two-Lipschitz property of regret gives
\[
|R_r(h,\delta)-R_r(g,\delta)|
\le\left(2+\frac{R_0\sqrt d}{2\sqrt{\lambda_0}}\right)\lVert h-g\rVert_\infty.
\]
Therefore finitely supported priors are weakly dense without changing Bayes values by more than the right-hand modulus, proving that their supremum already equals \(L(r)\).

Finally, \(r\mapsto\Sigma(r)\) is continuous on \([\rho,1]^{2K}\). The Gaussian covariance formula and the entropy-to-total-variation inequality above imply uniform total-variation continuity over \(h\in\mathcal H\); taking infima and suprema preserves this modulus, so \(L\) is continuous. The set \(\mathcal R_B\) is nonempty, closed, and bounded, hence compact. Every minimizing sequence has a convergent subsequence in \(\mathcal R_B\), and continuity makes its limit attain \(V^*\).

The first paragraph of the claim is exactly the defining list of member properties of \(\mathfrak C_{\mathrm H}\). At \(\omega_0\), \(h_3=0\) and \(h=(0,0)\) gives equal welfare to all three labels, so the finite-menu argmax is \([3]\). Every relative neighborhood of zero in \([-1,1]^2\) contains, respectively, points with \(h_1>\max(h_2,0)\), with \(h_2>\max(h_1,0)\), and with \(0>\max(h_1,h_2)\); hence each policy is uniquely optimal arbitrarily close to the tie.

If the asserted injective representation existed, evaluation at \(h=0\) would give the optimizer set \(\{\iota_{\mathrm H}(1),\iota_{\mathrm H}(2),\iota_{\mathrm H}(3)\}\). Injectivity makes these three points distinct, contradicting the singleton condition in the definition of \(\mathfrak C_{\mathrm H}\). Thus no smooth unique-optimum instance preserves this labelled choice correspondence.

The nuisance dimension is obtained directly from the saturated tangent:
\[
2K(L-1)-d=2\cdot4\cdot2-2=14.
\]
By \(\mathrm{lem:efficient\text{-}contrast\text{-}information}\), projection through \(\Pi_r\) produces \(\Sigma(r)\). At the witness, stratum three has \(d_3=(1,1)^\top\), so its strictly positive contribution has a positive off-diagonal entry; hence the covariance is design-dependent and non-diagonal. These are respectively the tie-geometry and selective-observation obstructions claimed.

Let the deterministic limiting rate of \(\mathcal A\) be \(r\). For any finite prior \(\nu=\sum_sw_s\delta_{h_s}\), the least-favourable lifts \(\mathcal T_rh_s\) differ from \(S_0h_s\) by elements of \(\ker(A_{\mathrm{tan}})=\operatorname{im}(W)\). Because the prior is finite, their nuisance coordinates lie in one ball \(\lVert v\rVert\le C(\nu)\). The supremum defining \(\mathcal R_-(\mathcal A)\) contains this submodel for every \(C_v\ge C(\nu)\). The finite-prior transfer in \(\mathrm{thm:nuisance\text{-}uniform\text{-}experiment}\), applied to the particular terminal rule of \(\mathcal A\), therefore yields
\[
\mathcal R_-(\mathcal A)\ge B_r(\nu),
\]
where \(B_r(\nu)\) is the Bayes regret in \(N(h,\Sigma(r))\). Taking the supremum over finite priors and invoking \(\mathrm{thm:gaussian\text{-}value\text{-}characterization}\) gives
\[
\mathcal R_-(\mathcal A)\ge\sup_{\nu\ {\rm finite}}B_r(\nu)=L(r).
\]
No convergence or regularity of the terminal selector was used: the Bayes envelope lower-bounds every measurable selector. Finally \(r\in\mathcal R_B\) and the definition \(V^*=\min_{s\in\mathcal R_B}L(s)\) imply \(L(r)\ge V^*\).

Let an effectively represented instance be fixed. The floor \(r_{ax}\ge\rho\), eta positivity, distinct support values, and \(\operatorname{rank}(F)=d\) give computable constants
\[
0<\lambda_0:=\lambda_{\min}\{\Sigma(\mathbf1)\}
\le\lambda_{\min}\{\Sigma(r)\},\qquad
\lambda_{\max}\{\Sigma(r)\}\le
\Lambda_0:=\lambda_{\max}\{\Sigma(\rho\mathbf1)\}.
\]
Writing \(H_{ax}=p_x\sigma^2_{ax}(q^0)d_xd_x^\top/e_{ax}\), direct differentiation of \(1/r_{ax}\) gives
\[
\lVert\Sigma(r)-\Sigma(s)\rVert_F
\le C_r\lVert r-s\rVert_\infty,
\qquad C_r=\rho^{-2}\sum_{a,x}\lVert H_{ax}\rVert_F.
\]
If \(S,T\succeq\lambda_0I\) and \(\lVert T-S\rVert_F\le\lambda_0/2\), put \(E=S^{-1/2}(T-S)S^{-1/2}\). Since \(\lVert E\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le1/2\) and \(u-\log(1+u)\le u^2\) for \(|u|\le1/2\),
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\{N(h,T),N(h,S)\}
\le\frac12\lVert E\rVert_F^2.
\]
The elementary entropy-to-total-variation inequality proved in the Gaussian-characterization argument therefore yields
\[
d_{\mathrm{TV}}\{N(h,T),N(h,S)\}
\le\frac{\lVert T-S\rVert_F}{2\lambda_0}.
\]
With \(U=\max_{h\in\mathcal H}\lVert h\rVert_\infty\) and \(R_0=2U\), the loss is bounded by \(R_0\) and is two-Lipschitz in \(h\). Equal-covariance Gaussian shifts similarly give the uniform state modulus
\[
|R(h,\delta)-R(g,\delta)|
\le K_H\lVert h-g\rVert_\infty,
\qquad K_H=2+\frac{R_0\sqrt d}{2\sqrt{\lambda_0}}.
\]

The projection \(P_B\) is the identity on \(\mathcal R_B\) and maps the full box onto it. If \(B=\rho\) it is constant. If \(B>\rho\), its two smooth pieces and matching boundary have the computable sup-norm Lipschitz bound \(1+(1-\rho)/(B-\rho)\). Thus a rational full-box mesh gives a finite certified covering mesh of \(\mathcal R_B\). The preceding covariance bound turns its covering radius \(\delta_r\) into design error
\[
E_{\mathrm{des}}=\frac{R_0C_r\delta_r}{2\lambda_0}.
\]

Choose \(T>U\). Every relevant Gaussian has
\[
P\{Z\notin[-T,T]^d\}\le2d\exp\left\{-\frac{(T-U)^2}{2\Lambda_0}\right\}=:p_T.
\]
Tile the cube exactly by rational cubes of side \(\gamma\). Coordinatewise averaging is an \(L^1\)-contraction, and the fundamental theorem of calculus gives
\[
\lVert f-\bar f\rVert_1
\le\gamma\sum_{j=1}^d\lVert\partial_jf\rVert_1
\le\frac{d\gamma}{\sqrt{\lambda_0}}.
\]
Consequently every measurable rule has a rectangle-constant approximation, with one fixed outside action, whose risk differs uniformly by at most
\[
E_{\mathrm{obs}}=R_0\left(p_T+\frac{d\gamma}{\sqrt{\lambda_0}}\right).
\]

At one design-grid point, let \(v(r)\) be the finite zero-sum game value using a \(\xi\)-net of \(\mathcal H\) and these observation rectangles. The two approximation directions are
\[
v(r)-E_{\mathrm{obs}}\le L(r)\le v(r)+K_H\xi.
\]
Indeed, averaging an arbitrary rule proves the left inequality, whereas evaluating the optimal rectangle rule at a nearest state-net point proves the right one. Each Gaussian rectangle probability is enclosed by \(\operatorname{GRect}\). Cholesky conditioning reduces the integral to a compact iterated integral after tails of total mass at most \(\zeta_{\mathrm{tail}}\) are removed. On that compact set all required Gaussian derivatives have explicit finite algebraic bounds; repeated subdivision therefore makes the quadrature width at most \(\zeta_{\mathrm{quad}}\), and increasing interval precision makes accumulated rounding width at most \(\zeta_{\mathrm{round}}\). Hence every call terminates with the asserted outward width.

The resulting finite linear program has rational interval coefficients. Rational primal and dual feasible vectors certify lower and upper values by weak duality; subdivision and increased precision reduce their gap to any prescribed \(E_{\mathrm{LP}}>0\). If the maximum rowwise probability-enclosure error is \(e_P\), its risk contribution is at most \(E_P=R_0e_P\). If \(v_{\mathrm{grid}}\) is the smallest certified finite-game value on the design grid, the proved global enclosure is
\[
v_{\mathrm{grid}}-E_{\mathrm{obs}}-E_{\mathrm{des}}-E_{\mathrm{LP}}-E_P
\le V^*\le
v_{\mathrm{grid}}+K_H\xi+E_{\mathrm{LP}}+E_P.
\]
Every term is effective and tends to zero under refinement. Enumerating refinements until their sum is at most \(\varepsilon\) therefore terminates and returns an interval of width at most \(\varepsilon\), together with the displayed feasible grid design and its certified rule.

Finally cover \(\mathcal R_B\) by the finitely many projected design cells. For each cell, subtract \(E_{\mathrm{des}}\) for its verified radius from its finite-game lower bound, and discard the cell only if this lower bound exceeds the global upper bound. A true minimizer can never be discarded, so the surviving finite union contains every minimizer. This is an objective certificate only; no distance-to-optimizer assertion has been used. Opaque reals or an unrepresented compact set do not permit the enumerations above, exactly as excluded in the claim.

Use the measurable procedure furnished by \(\mathrm{thm:coupled\text{-}measurable\text{-}attainment}\): fully label the independent pilot, select \(\widehat r_n\in\mathcal R_B\), annotate main-wave records independently at those rates, compute \(\widetilde\theta_n\), and apply its rectangle-constant Gaussian rule to the signal \(\sqrt n\,\widetilde\theta_n\). Pilot vanishing, feasibility, and \(\widehat r_n\to r^\dagger\) show that this sequence is an element \(\mathcal A^*\in\mathfrak A_{\mathrm{det}}\), with exactly the stated stabilized tree path.

Let \(c_{ax}=p_xe_{ax}\), \(\beta_n=\beta(q_n(h,v))\), and \(b=\beta_n-\widehat\beta\). Conditional on \(\mathscr P_n\), define the cell vector
\[
H_i(c)=\frac{\mathbf1\{X_i=x,A_i=a,R_i=1\}}{c_{ax}\widehat r_{n,ax}}
(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}-\widehat\beta_{ax}).
\]
Annotation ignorability gives \(E(H_i\mid\mathscr P_n)=b\), so \(\widetilde\beta_n\) is exactly conditionally unbiased for \(\beta_n\). Since only one cell coordinate can be nonzero,
\[
\operatorname{Var}(H_i\mid\mathscr P_n)
=\operatorname{diag}_{a,x}\left\{
\frac{\sigma^2_{n,ax}+b_{ax}^2}{p_xe_{ax}\widehat r_{n,ax}}
\right\}-bb^\top.
\]
Therefore the exact conditional covariance of the contrast error is
\[
S_n=A_{\mathrm{map}}\left[
\operatorname{diag}_{a,x}\left\{
\frac{\sigma^2_{n,ax}}{p_xe_{ax}\widehat r_{n,ax}}
\right\}
+\operatorname{diag}_{a,x}\left\{
\frac{b_{ax}^2}{p_xe_{ax}\widehat r_{n,ax}}
\right\}-bb^\top\right]A_{\mathrm{map}}^\top.
\]
The last two terms form the covariance of the random vector with coordinates \(b_c\mathbf1\{C=c,R=1\}/(c_c\widehat r_{n,c})\), hence are positive semidefinite. Pilot concentration gives \(\lVert b\rVert=O_P(m_n^{-1/2}+n^{-1/2})\) uniformly on a fixed nuisance fiber, and the affine local chart gives \(\max_c|\sigma^2_{n,c}-\sigma^2_c(q^0)|=O(n^{-1/2})\). Consequently
\[
\lVert S_n-\Sigma(\widehat r_n)\rVert
=O_P(m_n^{-1}+n^{-1/2})=o_P(1),
\qquad S_n\to_P\Sigma(r^\dagger).
\]

The summands are uniformly bounded because \(Y\) is bounded and \(p_x,e_{ax},\widehat r_{n,ax}\) have positive floors. Menu rank and the variance floor give a uniform positive lower covariance eigenvalue. Thus \(\mathrm{lem:bentkus\text{-}convex\text{-}set}\), conditionally on the pilot, proves
\[
\sqrt n\{\widetilde\theta_n-\theta_p(q_n(h,v))\}\Rightarrow
N(0,\Sigma(r^\dagger))
\]
uniformly on every fixed bounded nuisance fiber. The coupled theorem's rectangle count makes the same normal approximation valid for its changing rule, and its covariance and numerical errors vanish. Since \(\sqrt n\theta_p(q_n(h,v))=h\), the conditional risk is at most
\[
L(\widehat r_n)+o_P(1)=V^*+o_P(1),
\]
uniformly on that fiber. Bounded regret converts convergence in probability to convergence of expectations. Taking first \(n\to\infty\) for fixed \(C_v\), and only then \(C_v\to\infty\), gives \(\mathcal R_+(\mathcal A^*)\le V^*\). The converse \(\mathcal R_-(\mathcal A)\ge V^*\) for every admissible procedure was proved in \(\mathrm{thm:local\text{-}minimax\text{-}lower\text{-}bound}\); hence both deterministic-limit envelopes equal \(V^*\).

At \(\omega_0\), the fourth stratum has \(d_4=0\), while \(d_1=(1,0)^\top\), \(d_2=(0,1)^\top\), and \(d_3=(1,1)^\top\). Symmetrizing the two arm rates within a stratum preserves annotation cost and, by strict convexity of \(r\mapsto1/r\), weakly decreases each stratum's covariance coefficient. With symmetric useful-stratum rates write
\[
a=\frac{0.03}{r_1},\qquad b=\frac{0.30}{r_2},\qquad c=\frac{0.25}{r_3};
\quad
\Sigma=\begin{pmatrix}a+c&c\\c&b+c\end{pmatrix},
\quad G=\max\{a+c,b+c,a+b\}.
\]
Put \(\alpha=9/634\). The supporting objective
\[
H_\alpha=\alpha(a+b)+(1-\alpha)(b+c)
\]
is no larger than \(G\). It is strictly convex in all six useful arm rates. Its budget-constrained first-order equations, with the agreement-stratum rates at their floor, have the unique solution
\[
s=\frac{\sqrt{634}}{25},\qquad
r_{3G}=\frac{529/1000}{317/1250+(3/10)s},\qquad
r_{2G}=sr_{3G},\qquad r_{1G}=\frac3{25}r_{3G},\qquad r_{4G}=\frac1{20}.
\]
At this point \(a=c<b\), so \(H_\alpha=a+b=b+c=G\). Thus the lower bound \(H_\alpha\le G\) is attained at its unique minimizer. Strict convexity, including the equality condition in arm symmetrization, proves that the full eight-coordinate optimizer set \(\mathcal G(\omega_0)\) is the singleton consisting of this arm-symmetric design.

For the regret lower certificate use the prior with atoms
\[
(-5/8,-5/8),\quad(0,5/8),\quad(5/8,0)
\]
and weights \((13/40,7/20,13/40)\). At each atom every incorrect action has regret \(5/8\). If \(P_{kk}\) is the probability that the Gaussian Bayes discriminant selects the correct atom, its Bayes risk is
\[
B_G=\frac58\left(1-\sum_kw_kP_{kk}\right)\le L_{\omega_0}(r_G).
\]
Writing \(\beta_k=\Sigma(r_G)^{-1}h^k\) and \(b_k=\log w_k-(h^k)^\top\Sigma(r_G)^{-1}h^k/2\), each \(P_{kk}\) is the probability of two affine Gaussian inequalities. Direct differentiation of the bivariate normal integral in its correlation parameter gives
\[
\Phi_2(u,v;q)=\Phi(u)\Phi(v)+\int_0^q\phi_2(u,v;t)\,dt.
\]
For \(|t|\le q_*<1\), diagonalization and \(\sup_z z^2e^{-z^2/2}=2/e\) give
\[
|\partial_t\phi_2(u,v;t)|
\le\frac{q_*+2/e}{2\pi(1-q_*^2)^{3/2}}.
\]
Thus \(N\)-panel midpoint quadrature has outward error at most \(q_*^2\) times this bound divided by \(4N\). With \(N=512\) and 96-bit outward interval arithmetic, the resulting rational-endpoint enclosure proves \(B_G>0.1965\).

For the feasible alternative, exact arithmetic gives
\[
\sum_xp_xr^0_{\mathrm{alt},x}=\frac{11}{20},\qquad
\Sigma(r^0_{\mathrm{alt}})=
\begin{pmatrix}433/1205&125/482\\125/482&8695/14942\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Use the feasible rule selecting the largest of \(z_1,z_2,0\). Its selection probabilities are bivariate normal quadrant probabilities, so the same identity with \(N=64\) encloses its risk. On a square of sup-norm half-width \(w\), the state-risk modulus is
\[
2+\frac{\sqrt2}{\sqrt{\lambda_{\min}\{\Sigma(r^0_{\mathrm{alt}})\}}}.
\]
An outward-rounded dyadic cover of \([-1,1]^2\), with \(74107\) accepted leaves and maximum depth ten, gives the global upper enclosure
\[
\sup_{h\in[-1,1]^2}R(h)<0.184529576390235<0.18453.
\]
All tail probabilities are full Gaussian quadrant probabilities, so no observation truncation is hidden. The finite interval operations are certified by \(\mathrm{thm:certified\text{-}computation}\). Therefore
\[
L_{\omega_0}(r_G)>0.1965,\qquad
L_{\omega_0}(r_{\mathrm{alt}}(\omega_0))<0.18453,
\]
and the regret gap exceeds \(0.1965-0.18453=0.01197\). Since a feasible design has smaller regret, no minimizer of \(L_{\omega_0}\) equals the unique \(G\)-minimizer.

Write \(\sigma_{ax}=\sqrt{\sigma^2_{ax}(q^{0,\omega})}\), \(S_x=\sigma_{0x}+\sigma_{1x}\), and \(A_x=p_x^\omega S_x^2\). For a fixed average arm rate \(t_x=(r_{0x}+r_{1x})/2\), Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
2p_x^\omega\sum_{a=0}^1\frac{\sigma_{ax}^2}{r_{ax}}
\ge\frac{p_x^\omega S_x^2}{t_x}=\frac{A_x}{t_x},
\]
with equality only at \(r_{ax}=2t_x\sigma_{ax}/S_x\). Put
\[
C_{13}=p_1^\omega A_1+p_3^\omega A_3,\quad C_2=p_2^\omega A_2,\quad
C=B^\omega-\rho p_4^\omega,
\]
\[
z=\frac{(\sqrt{C_{13}}+\sqrt{C_2})\sqrt{C_{13}}}{C},\qquad
y=\frac{(\sqrt{C_{13}}+\sqrt{C_2})\sqrt{C_2}}{C},\qquad
t_1=A_1/z,\quad t_2=A_2/y,\quad t_3=A_3/z.
\]
The interval bounds defining \(\mathcal U_{10^{-6}}\) verify \(\rho<2t_x\sigma_{ax}/S_x<1\), \(z<y\), and \(0<p_1^\omega A_1/C_{13}<1\). Repeating the strictly convex supporting-objective proof from \(\mathrm{thm:witness\text{-}separation}\), now with weight \(p_1^\omega A_1/C_{13}\), proves that these arm rates, together with \(r_{a4}=\rho\), are the unique member of \(\mathcal G(\omega)\).

For the competitor, applying \(P_\omega\) to the arm-symmetric vector gives
\[
r_{\mathrm{alt},ax}(\omega)=\rho+\kappa_\omega(r^0_{\mathrm{alt},x}-\rho),\qquad
\kappa_\omega=\frac{B^\omega-\rho}{\sum_xp_x^\omega r^0_{\mathrm{alt},x}-\rho}.
\]
The same interval box proves \(0<r_{\mathrm{alt},ax}(\omega)<1\) and exact budget equality, hence feasibility. Outward arithmetic on the entire closed radius-\(10^{-6}\) box, which contains the relative open neighborhood in the claim, gives
\[
\lVert\Sigma_\omega(r_G(\omega))-\Sigma_{\omega_0}(r_G)\rVert_F
\le4.0459382\times10^{-5},
\]
\[
\lVert\Sigma_\omega(r_{\mathrm{alt}}(\omega))-\Sigma_{\omega_0}(r^0_{\mathrm{alt}})\rVert_F
\le1.2428859\times10^{-5}.
\]
The covariance total-variation bound proved in \(\mathrm{thm:certified\text{-}computation}\), multiplied by the prior loss bound \(5/8\) for the lower certificate and by the square loss bound two for the upper rule, propagates the center certificates to
\[
L_\omega(r_G(\omega))>0.1964558818>0.1964558,
\]
and
\[
L_\omega(r_{\mathrm{alt}}(\omega))<0.1845959638<0.1845960.
\]
The middle numerical inequality \(0.1964558>0.1845960\) is exact decimal arithmetic. Finally, every allowed standard deviation is realized on the fixed ternary support by
\[
q^{0,\omega}_{ax}=(\sigma_{ax}^2/2,\,1-\sigma_{ax}^2,\,\sigma_{ax}^2/2),
\]
whose coordinates remain above \(\eta=1/10\) throughout the box and whose mean is zero. Thus the neighborhood is nonempty and remains inside the stipulated saturated causal model.

When \(M=2\), \(d=1\), the Gaussian game in \(\mathrm{def:gaussian\text{-}game}\) observes \(N(h,\Sigma(r))\). By the definition of the binary benchmark this is exactly \(L_{\sqrt{\Sigma(r)}}(\mathcal H)\). If \(Z=h+\sigma\varepsilon\), divide by \(\sigma\) and write \(g=h/\sigma\). Positive homogeneity of regret gives \(\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}(h,j)=\sigma\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}(g,j)\), while \(Z/\sigma\sim N(g,1)\). Taking the same infimum and supremum after this bijective reparameterization yields
\[
L_\sigma(\mathcal H)=\sigma L_1(\mathcal H/\sigma).
\]
If \(0<\sigma_1\le\sigma_2\), generate independently \(E\sim N(0,\sigma_2^2-\sigma_1^2)\). From \(Z_1\sim N(h,\sigma_1^2)\), the randomized rule \(E\mapsto\delta_2(Z_1+E)\) has exactly the risk of any prescribed rule \(\delta_2\) in the \(\sigma_2\)-experiment. Thus the smaller-noise experiment can reproduce every larger-noise risk vector, and
\[
L_{\sigma_1}(\mathcal H)\le L_{\sigma_2}(\mathcal H).
\]
Consequently a design minimizing the sole scalar variance also minimizes binary regret. The simulation argument gives only weak monotonicity, so it makes neither of the disclaimed assertions.

theorem.statement: There is a jointly measurable implementation of \(\mathrm{def:implementation\text{-}handle}\) with the stipulated coordinate order, parent-only recursion, lexicographic child order, and separate testing of every closed child containing a shared-boundary point. For each fixed depth \(k\), its selected ambient boxes and feasible cells equal \(\mathcal D_j^\dagger\) and \(\mathcal C_j^\dagger\), respectively, for all \(j\le k\) with probability tending to one locally uniformly on every bounded nuisance fiber. Define the population prefix gaps \(\gamma_j(L)\) as in the proof and let \(j_n(L)\) be the largest certified depth for which the approximation envelope is smaller than all preceding positive prefix gaps. Then \(a_n(L)=\sup_{m\ge n}2^{-j_m(L)}\downarrow0\) and \(\lVert\widehat r_n-r^\dagger\rVert=O_P(a_n(L))\) locally uniformly. This conclusion includes disconnected, flat, tied, and dyadic-boundary minimizing sets. A jointly refined rectangle-constant Gaussian rule has risk error \(o(1)\) uniformly over every fixed bounded nuisance fiber. No nontrivial law-uniform spatial rate follows from the stated assumptions alone: without a uniform prefix-separation or optimizer-identification modulus, uniformly accurate objective values can correspond to canonically selected minimizers a fixed positive distance apart.
theorem.proof_tex:
Set
\[
b_n=\left\{\frac{\log(n+1)}{m_n}\right\}^{1/2}+n^{-1/2},
\qquad t_n=b_n^{1/2}.
\]
The pilot assumptions imply \(b_n\to0\), \(t_n\to0\), and \(b_n=o(t_n)\). Fully labelled pilot cell frequencies, means, and second moments obey bounded exponential-moment inequalities. Because there are finitely many cells, clipping to the eta-implied positive variance interval gives, locally uniformly on every fixed bounded fiber,
\[
\max_{a,x}|\widehat\sigma^2_{ax}-\sigma^2_{ax}(q^0)|=O_P(b_n),
\]
with a bad-event probability tending to zero uniformly. The local law differs from \(q^0\) by \(O(n^{-1/2})\), which is already included in \(b_n\). The covariance and Gaussian-risk moduli proved in \(\mathrm{thm:certified\text{-}computation}\) then give
\[
\sup_{r\in\mathcal R_B}|\widehat L_n(r)-L(r)|\le Cb_n
\]
on the same high-probability event, for a deterministic structural constant \(C\).

Let \(k_n=\lfloor\log_2\log(n+2)\rfloor\). For every feasible closed dyadic child encountered through depth \(k_n\), approximate its plug-in minimum with numerical error and design covering modulus at most \(t_n^2/16\) each. On represented instances this is exactly the certified solver with the child's additional rational box constraints, and every call terminates. For an arbitrary fixed mathematical instance, fix once and for all a countable dense subset of each compact feasible child and use a sufficiently long finite prefix; the infimum of the continuous plug-in objective over that dense subset equals its compact minimum, and finite minima of measurable functions are measurable. Thus this alternative defines the same measurable theoretical procedure without making an extra computability claim. Let \(\widehat v_{n,j,b}\) be the resulting approximate cell minimum. All later operations are finite comparisons, so choosing the lexicographically first retained child is measurable. Write \(\bar\alpha_n=Cb_n+t_n^2/8=O(b_n)=o(t_n)\). On the pilot good event,
\[
|\widehat v_{n,j,b}-v_{j,b}|\le\bar\alpha_n
\]
simultaneously for the finitely many tested children, where \(v_{j,b}\) is the corresponding population cell minimum. Retain precisely those siblings satisfying
\[
\widehat v_{n,j,b}\le\min_c\widehat v_{n,j,c}+t_n,
\]
and recurse only inside the unique selected parent. The sibling attaining the finite empirical minimum is retained, so the empirical cells are nonempty and nested. Choose the first certified feasible grid point in the final selected cell and call its projection \(\widehat r_n\).

For the children of the population parent \(\mathcal D_{j-1}^\dagger\), put
\[
E_j=\{b:v_{j,b}=V^*\},\qquad
\gamma_j(L)=\min_{b\notin E_j}(v_{j,b}-V^*),
\]
with \(\gamma_j(L)=+\infty\) if every feasible child is in \(E_j\). The set of siblings is finite and every ineligible child is compact and disjoint from the minimizer set, so \(\gamma_j(L)>0\). If the empirical parent is correct, \(2\bar\alpha_n<t_n\) implies that every child in \(E_j\) is retained, while
\[
t_n+2\bar\alpha_n<\gamma_j(L)
\]
implies that no child outside \(E_j\) is retained. The lexicographically first retained child is therefore exactly the population child. Induction proves stabilization of every fixed prefix. If a minimizer lies on a shared boundary, each closed child containing it belongs to \(E_j\) and is tested separately, so the same argument selects the stipulated first one. Flat or disconnected minimizer sets merely enlarge \(E_j\) and do not affect the proof.

The outward lower and upper cell-value bounds of \(\mathrm{thm:certified\text{-}computation}\) converge to each \(v_{j,b}\). Hence every strictly positive \(\gamma_j(L)\) is eventually accompanied by a positive certified lower bound, and the sequence of such bounds is the advertised certified prefix-separation profile.

Define
\[
j_n(L)=\max\left\{j\le k_n:
t_n+2\bar\alpha_n<\min_{1\le i\le j}\gamma_i(L)\right\},
\qquad a_n(L)=\sup_{m\ge n}2^{-j_m(L)},
\]
with the empty maximum equal to zero. Each fixed finite minimum on the right is positive and \(k_n\to\infty\), so \(j_n(L)\to\infty\). It follows directly that the displayed tail supremum is nonincreasing and tends to zero. On the good event, the empirical and population paths agree through depth \(j_n(L)\); both \(\widehat r_n\) and \(r^\dagger\) lie in that feasible cell. Therefore
\[
\lVert\widehat r_n-r^\dagger\rVert
\le\sqrt{2K}(1-\rho)2^{-j_n(L)}
\le\sqrt{2K}(1-\rho)a_n(L),
\]
which is the claimed locally uniform \(O_P(a_n(L))\) rate.

For the decision component, at refinement level \(s\) use the certified state net, a truncation cube, and finitely many rational observation rectangles, and let their total deterministic approximation error be at most \(2^{-s}\). Choose a deterministic \(s_n\uparrow\infty\) slowly enough that the number \(J_n\) of rectangles is \(o(\sqrt n)\). Conditional on the pilot, the standardized AIPW summands are independent, centered, uniformly bounded, and have covariance eigenvalues bounded away from zero by the annotation floor and menu rank. The convex-set bound in \(\mathrm{lem:bentkus\text{-}convex\text{-}set}\) is therefore \(O(n^{-1/2})\) for every rectangle. The risk difference for a rule constant on \(J_n\) rectangles is at most \(2R_0J_nO(n^{-1/2})=o(1)\). Covariance-estimation, Gaussian-tail, state-mesh, quadrature, and linear-program errors also vanish by construction. All bounds are uniform on each fixed bounded nuisance fiber, which establishes the coupled risk statement.

Finally, the dependence on \(\gamma_j(L)\) cannot be removed under mere continuity. On \([0,1]\), for any \(\epsilon>0\), the two continuous objectives \(f_+(z)=\epsilon z\) and \(f_-(z)=\epsilon(1-z)\) have canonical minimizers zero and one, yet the single approximation \(g(z)=\epsilon/2\) is within \(\epsilon/2\) uniformly of both. Hence no procedure seeing only an error-\(\epsilon/2\) objective approximation can locate both canonical minimizers within distance less than \(1/2\). Since \(\epsilon\) can decrease arbitrarily slowly, a law-uniform spatial rate requires an additional lower bound on prefix gaps, or equivalently an optimizer-identification modulus. This generic certificate does not weaken the law-specific rate just proved.
theorem.justification: The construction gives a measurable deterministic-limit selector and a law-specific spatial rate at every nonunique optimum.
theorem.gap: The rate necessarily depends on the objective's prefix-separation profile; the proof gives an explicit generic certificate showing why no law-uniform spatial rate follows without an identification modulus.
theorem.consumer: This theorem supplies the implementable design and decision schedule required by the attainment theorem.

added_lemmas.statement: For a row-wise independent triangular array of centered random vectors of fixed finite dimension, convergence of the summed covariance matrices together with the Lindeberg condition implies convergence in distribution of the row sums to the centered normal law with the limiting covariance.

attestation.note: Specialized from the cited Lindeberg--Feller proposition; stable publisher DOI supplied in place of a verbatim transcription.

added_lemmas.statement: For every finite measure \(\mu\), the closed unit ball of \(L^\infty(\mu)=(L^1(\mu))^*\) is compact in the weak-star topology.

attestation.note: Banach--Alaoglu compactness specialized to the dual of an L1 space; stable DOI supplied in place of a verbatim transcription.

added_lemmas.statement: If one strategy set is compact and convex, the other is convex, and the payoff is upper semicontinuous and concave in the compact-side variable and lower semicontinuous and convex in the other variable, then the maximum of the infima equals the infimum of the maxima.

attestation.note: The theorem is specialized to randomized decision rules and priors; stable journal DOI supplied in place of a verbatim transcription.

added_lemmas.statement: Let independent centered random vectors in a fixed finite dimension have identity summed covariance. The supremum, over convex Borel sets, of the absolute difference between the distribution of their sum and the standard Gaussian distribution is at most \(400\) times the fourth root of the dimension times the sum of their third Euclidean absolute moments.

attestation.note: Specialized from Bentkus's convex-set multivariate Berry--Esseen theorem; stable DOI supplied in place of a verbatim transcription.

proposed.statement:
Fix \(r\in\mathcal R_B\), \(C_v<\infty\), and \(\mathcal A\in\mathfrak A_{\mathrm{det}}\) whose pilot-measurable main-wave rate \(\widehat r_n\) converges locally uniformly in probability to \(r\). The strict slack \(\delta_q>0\) implies that, for all sufficiently large \(n\), every positive or negative tilt on \(\mathcal H\times\{v:\lVert v\rVert\le C_v\}\) lies in \(\mathcal M_\eta(p)\). Conditional on \(\mathscr P_n\), every fixed finite collection of points in that domain obeys the observed-data expansion
\[
\log\frac{d(\mathbb P^{\widehat r_n}_{p,q_n(h,v)})^{\otimes n}}{d(\mathbb P^{\widehat r_n}_{p,q^0})^{\otimes n}}(O_1,\ldots,O_n)
=\Delta_n(s(h,v))-\tfrac12J_{\widehat r_n}(s(h,v),s(h,v))+\operatorname{rem}_{n,\widehat r_n}(h,v),
\]
where \(\sup_{h\in\mathcal H,\lVert v\rVert\le C_v}|\operatorname{rem}_{n,\widehat r_n}(h,v)|=o_{\mathbb P^{\widehat r_n}_{p,q^0}}(1)\). Under \(\mathbb P^{\widehat r_n}_{p,q^0}\), the conditional finite-coordinate law of \(\Delta_n\) converges to a centered Gaussian process with covariance \(J_r\), uniformly on that compact domain. The map \(\Pi_rs=\mathcal T_rA_{\mathrm{tan}}s\) is the \(J_r\)-orthogonal contrast projection, and under \(\mathbb P^{\widehat r_n}_{p,q_n(h,v)}\), \(U_{n,r}\Rightarrow N(h,\Sigma(r))\) uniformly on the same domain. The likelihood contribution from \(\mathscr P_n\), whose fully labeled pilot records satisfy \(R=1\) and \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}=Y\), is asymptotically negligible because \(m_n/n\to0\). Consequently, for every finite prior on \(\mathcal H\), the infimum over all \(\psi_n\) of the prior regret along the least-favorable submodels \(q^0+\mathcal T_rh/\sqrt n\), which also remain in \(\mathcal M_\eta(p)\) for both signs and all sufficiently large \(n\) by the same slack argument, converges to the Bayes regret in \(Z\sim N(h,\Sigma(r))\); this finite-prior risk-transfer conclusion, rather than total-variation convergence of experiments, is the conclusion used downstream.
proposed.justification: The explicit conditional LAN expansion and finite-prior transfer identify exactly what survives a discontinuous pilot design and the complete contrast-preserving nuisance fiber.
proposed.gap: Hirano and Porter provide fixed-experiment scalar treatment-rule transfer, while Cook et al. provide stabilized adaptive AIPW Gaussianity; neither conditions on a pilot sigma-field to prove a design-indexed finite-coordinate LAN expansion and least-favorable finite-prior transfer over all outcome-shape tangents.
proposed.consumer: It licenses lower-risk transfer for any admissible prospective annotation procedure and prevents a restricted outcome family from determining the design.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proof invokes the classical finite-dimensional Lindeberg--Feller theorem, so the cited leaf must be declared in the proof spine.

proposed.statement: For every \(r\in\mathcal R_B\), the full-fiber Gaussian minimax regret equals \(L(r)\); the infimum over \(\delta\) is attained, \(L\) is continuous on \(\mathcal R_B\), and \(V^*=\min_{r\in\mathcal R_B}L(r)\) is attained. The value also equals the supremum of finite-prior Bayes values over \(\mathcal H\).
proposed.justification: This identifies the design objective and establishes that both the terminal rule and annotation optimum exist.
proposed.gap: Masten and Kato analyze many-action games for treatment arms; the theorem concerns correlated overlapping policy values whose covariance is chosen through selective outcome observation.
proposed.consumer: Prospective validators obtain a well-defined population target instead of a collection of unrelated contrast variances.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The existence and minimax-equality proof uses weak-star compactness and Sion's minimax theorem, which must be explicit cited leaves.

proposed.statement: A solution of \(\mathrm{oeq:coupled\text{-}measurable\text{-}attainment}\), combined with \(\widetilde\theta_n\), yields \(\mathcal A^*\in\mathfrak A_{\mathrm{det}}\) whose empirical selected ambient box at depth \(k+1\) is the lexicographically first eligible closed child of its unique depth-\(k\) selected ambient box under the fixed arm-within-stratum coordinate order, with shared-boundary children tested separately and no unrelated cell eligible. Every fixed empirical prefix stabilizes to \(\mathcal D_k^\dagger\), its feasible cells stabilize to the nested population cells \(\mathcal C_k^\dagger\), and \(\widehat r_n\to r^\dagger\) locally uniformly in probability, where \(\{r^\dagger\}=\bigcap_{k=0}^{\infty}\mathcal C_k^\dagger\). Moreover, \(\sqrt n\{\widetilde\theta_n-\theta_p(q_n(h,v))\}\Rightarrow N(0,\Sigma(r^\dagger))\) uniformly over every fixed bounded nuisance fiber, and \(\mathcal R_+(\mathcal A^*)\le V^*\). Hence the lower and upper deterministic-limit local minimax envelopes both equal \(V^*\).
proposed.justification: The upper theorem matches the full-nuisance converse with an implementable pilot, joint estimator, and terminal rule.
proposed.gap: Nwankwo et al. attain scalar ATE variance and Cook et al. prove scalar adaptive AIPW limits; neither couples a set-valued regret design to a multivariate discontinuous minimax rule.
proposed.consumer: Independent validation of a frozen clinical-policy menu can target scarce follow-up toward the cells that minimize eventual welfare loss.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The changing-rectangle risk transfer uses Bentkus's convex-set normal approximation directly, so its cited leaf is added to the theorem's declared spine.

proposed.def: \(r_{\mathrm{alt}}(\omega)=P_\omega(r_{\mathrm{alt}}^0)\). At \(\omega_0\), exact arithmetic gives \(\sum_{x=1}^{4}\sum_{a=0}^{1}p_xe_{ax}r^0_{\mathrm{alt},ax}=11/20=B\). Thus \(r_{\mathrm{alt}}^0\) is feasible, its projection equals itself, and \(r_{\mathrm{alt}}(\omega_0)=r_{\mathrm{alt}}^0\).
